title: Split body, torso, head, and regional viewing direction
plainLanguage: A body can face mostly forward while the head turns to the side. One single “view” label is not enough for perspective-heavy character building.
purpose: Make viewpoint information precise enough to compare and later assemble compatible 2D pieces.

rules.statement: Record body/torso orientation and head orientation independently.
Allow region-specific orientation overrides when an arm or leg is strongly out of the torso plane.
Preserve MIXED and UNKNOWN rather than forcing one of the five main view families.
Keep screen heading separate from anatomical left/right.

implementation.currentSupport: Corpus Pane 0.2.2.4 stores body and head viewing direction separately, preserves prior head-direction observations, and uses the reviewed body view within the ordered FRONT → FRONT_THREE_QUARTER → PROFILE → BACK_THREE_QUARTER → BACK retrieval ladder.
implementation.futureWork: Regional overrides remain a later extension; continue testing split view labels across turns and occlusion-heavy clips.
